newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close firmer after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close firmer after choppy session.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed slightly firmer after a volatile session, with news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacked his security chief Alexander Lebed jolting markets in afternoon trading, dealers said. * General index up 2.05 points, 0.55 percent, to 376.82. * Ibex-35 index rose 26.80 points, 0.62 percent, to 4,322.27. * Telefonica gained 15 pesetas to 2,505 with more than three million shares traded. Repsol was down five pesetas at 4,450.
Traders said the market had see-sawed in line with bonds this session and although they predicted continued volatility, they were confident the indices could set new highs soon.

"After a relatively quiet morning, we have had an afternoon of continuous ups and downs with moments of directionless, but in the end buying pressure came through and we could soon see new historic levels," said a trader.
Volume was slightly more moderate than on Wednesday at 37.5 billion pesetas. Traders said the main focus for stocks on Friday was the expiry of futures contracts.
Large banks improved in afternoon trading, led by BBV which gained 1.2 percent. Electricity firms also rose after a recent bout of profit-taking.
